title: The English Alphabet
summary: All 26 letters of the English alphabet, one lesson each. Every letter teaches the uppercase and lowercase shapes, the real sound it makes inside words, and drills that run from hearing the letter to writing the word yourself.

lessons.title: The letter A
lessons.summary: Write and say A and a, then practise them in the word apple.

steps.heading: The letter A / a
steps.body:
Uppercase A is two slanting strokes joined by a crossbar in the middle. Lowercase a is a small round bowl with a short stem on the right. They are the same letter in two sizes: the tall printed form and the small written form, and both are read as the same sound /æ/ in words like apple.

The letter A is not pronounced as its own name inside a word. It has several sounds, and the common one is the short /æ/ you hear at the start of apple. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: A, a, A, a. The best example word for this letter is apple (quả táo).

rules.title: Uppercase and lowercase
rules.statement: English has two printed forms of every letter. The uppercase A is the tall form, used at the start of a sentence and for a proper name. The lowercase a is the small form, used everywhere else. Both forms represent the same letter, and in apple the letter is written a at the start of the word.

examples.note: The A in apple is the short /æ/ sound, as in the word cat. Do not say the letter name /eɪ/ inside the word.

examples.en: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
examples.vi: Một quả táo mỗi ngày giúp bạn khỏe, xa bác sĩ.
examples.note: a and a both use the short /æ/. The final word away is stressed on the second syllable: a-WAY.

rules.title: How the letter A is pronounced
rules.statement: The letter A is not pronounced as its own name inside a word. It has several sounds, and the common one is the short /æ/ you hear at the start of apple.

examples.note: The A in apple is the short /æ/ sound, as in the word cat. Do not say the letter name /eɪ/ inside the word.
The same letter A is read /ɑː/ in arm, not /æ/. The vowel sound of A depends on the letters that follow it.

lessons.title: The letter B
lessons.summary: Write and say B and b, then practise them in the word book.

steps.heading: The letter B / b
steps.body:
Uppercase B is one straight stem with two rounded bowls on the right. Lowercase b is a tall stem with one bowl in the lower half. Both forms are the same shape built from a stem and a bowl; the lowercase simply has only one bowl.

B is voiced: the voice vibrates in the throat while the lips touch, as in book. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: B, b, B, b. The best example word for this letter is book (cuốn sách).

The lowercase b is the small form, used everywhere else. Both forms represent the same letter, and in book the letter is written b at the start of the word.

examples.note: Both oo letters here are not special: book is /bʊk/, with the short vowel /ʊ/.

examples.en: A book is a friend that never lets you down.
examples.vi: Một cuốn sách là người bạn không bao giờ khiến bạn thất vọng.

lessons.title: The letter C
lessons.summary: Write and say C and c, then practise them in the word cat.

steps.heading: The letter C / c
steps.body:
Uppercase C is one open curve, like a wide crescent. Lowercase c is the same curve, drawn smaller. The two are the same curve at two sizes; C is simply the larger, straighter form.

Before a, o and u, C is hard /k/, as in cat. Before e, i and y it is soft /s/, as in city. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: C, c, C, c. The best example word for this letter is cat (con mèo).

examples.vi: Con mèo ngồi trên tấm thảm.

lessons.title: The letter D
lessons.summary: Write and say D and d, then practise them in the word dog.

steps.heading: The letter D / d
steps.body:
Uppercase D is a straight stem with one big half-circle on the right. Lowercase d is a round bowl with a tall stem rising on the right. The stem and the bowl are the same idea in both forms; the uppercase bowl is simply bigger.

D is voiced /d/ and usually sits next to a vowel, as in dog, where the little flap is added to the vowel. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: D, d, D, d. The best example word for this letter is dog (con chó).

rules.title: Uppercase and lowercase
rules.statement: English has two printed forms of every letter. The uppercase D is the tall form, used at the start of a sentence and for a proper name. The lowercase d is the small form, used everywhere else. Both forms represent the same letter, and in dog the letter is written d at the start of the word.

examples.note: The final g is a soft velar /ɡ/ made at the back of the mouth, and it is voiced.

examples.en: My dog runs fast in the park.
examples.vi: Chú chó của tôi chạy nhanh trong công viên.

lessons.title: The letter E
lessons.summary: Write and say E and e, then practise them in the word egg.

steps.heading: The letter E / e
steps.body:
Uppercase E is one straight stem with three horizontal bars. Lowercase e is a small loop with a horizontal crossbar, like a printed c with a bar. The lowercase e is the small, rounded relative of the tall E; the crossbar appears in both.

E is short /e/ in egg, as in bed, and long /iː/ in words like be. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: E, e, E, e. The best example word for this letter is egg (quả trứng).

lessons.title: The letter F
lessons.summary: Write and say F and f, then practise them in the word fish.

steps.heading: The letter F / f
steps.body:
Uppercase F is one stem, a bar at the top and a bar in the middle. Lowercase f has a tall curved hook at the top of the stem. Both forms are the same shape; the lowercase f is narrower and starts with a curve.

F is /f/, made by touching the lower lip to the upper teeth and letting air through. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: F, f, F, f. The best example word for this letter is fish (con cá).

rules.title: Uppercase and lowercase

The lowercase f is the small form, used everywhere else. Both forms represent the same letter, and in fish the letter is written f at the start of the word.

examples.note: The sh in fish makes one /ʃ/ sound; the two letters are not pronounced separately.

examples.vi: Con cá bơi trong làn nước trong.

G is hard /ɡ/ before a, o, u as in girl, and soft /dʒ/ before e, i, y as in gem. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: G, g, G, g. The best example word for this letter is girl (cô bé).

lessons.title: The letter H
lessons.summary: Write and say H and h, then practise them in the word hat.

steps.heading: The letter H / h
steps.body:
Uppercase H is two vertical stems joined by a middle bar. Lowercase h is a tall stem with one arch on the right. The two vertical strokes of the uppercase become the stem and the arch of the lowercase.

H is /h/, a soft breath, when it comes before a vowel, as in hat. In words like hour it is silent. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: H, h, H, h. The best example word for this letter is hat (chiếc mũ).

The lowercase h is the small form, used everywhere else. Both forms represent the same letter, and in hat the letter is written h at the start of the word.

examples.note: The a is the short /æ/ and the h is a soft /h/ breath; the two never blend into one sound.

examples.en: He put a hat on his head.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đội mũ lên đầu.
examples.note: The h in the is a soft /h/, while the h in head starts the stronger /h/ sound.

lessons.title: The letter I
lessons.summary: Write and say I and i, then practise them in the word ice.

steps.heading: The letter I / i
steps.body:
Uppercase I is one vertical stroke, sometimes with bars on top and bottom. Lowercase i is one short stroke with a dot above it. They differ only in size and in the dot; the stem is identical.

lessons.summary: Write and say J and j, then practise them in the word jump.

lessons.title: The letter Q
lessons.summary: Write and say Q and q, then practise them in the word queen.

steps.body:
Uppercase Q is a circle with a short tail crossing the bottom right. Lowercase q is a bowl with a tail descending on the right. The circle and the tail are the same in both forms; only the size and the height of the tail change.

lessons.title: The letter R
lessons.summary: Write and say R and r, then practise them in the word rain.

Uppercase R is a stem, one bowl and one diagonal leg. Lowercase r is a short stem with a small arm curving out at the top. The uppercase adds the leg to the stem and bowl; the lowercase is reduced to the stem and the little arm.

steps.heading: The letter Y / y
steps.body:
Uppercase Y is two arms meeting on a vertical stem. Lowercase y is the same shape with a tail that goes below the line. The arms and the stem stay the same; the lowercase tail is what makes it a y and not a u.

Y is the vowel /e/ at the start of a word, as in yellow. It is also the diphthong /aɪ/ at the end, as in my, and it is silent in happy. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: Y, y, Y, y. The best example word for this letter is yellow (màu vàng).

lessons.summary: Write and say Z and z, then practise them in the word zebra.

steps.heading: The letter Z / z
steps.body:
Uppercase Z is one top bar, one diagonal and one bottom bar. Lowercase z is the same three strokes, slightly smaller. The two bars and the diagonal are identical in both forms; only the size differs.

Z is voiced /z/ in zebra, with the same buzzing sound as the s in rose. In English the letter is named zed. Write the uppercase form first, then the lowercase form below it, and say the pair out loud: Z, z, Z, z. The best example word for this letter is zebra (con ngựa vằn).
